what: Tyson Foods is one of the world's largest meat companies. It processes chicken, beef and pork, and makes prepared foods under brands such as Jimmy Dean, Hillshire Farm and Ball Park.
customers: Supermarkets, restaurant chains, foodservice distributors and export buyers.
money: poultry processing, the most profitable segment recently
branded sausage, lunch meat and frozen products
moat: Processing plants and distribution at a scale few can match, with branded prepared foods that earn more than commodity meat.
risks: Beef margins have been deeply negative because cattle supply is at multi-decade lows
Net margin of about 1% leaves no room for error
Debt of about $8.7 billion against under $1 billion of cash
Return on invested capital of about 3%
opportunities: Chicken margins have been strong and offset beef losses
Prepared Foods brands are far more profitable than commodity processing
The cattle cycle will eventually turn, which would restore beef margins
watch: Beef segment operating margin and the cattle herd rebuilding cycle.
